# Feature Requirements: slugify-utility

## Overview

### Purpose
Provide a string utility function that converts arbitrary text into URL-safe, human-readable slugs suitable for use in web addresses, file names, and identifiers.

### Business Context
Slugs are essential for creating clean, SEO-friendly URLs and consistent identifiers across the application. This utility will standardize text transformation logic, ensuring consistent slug generation throughout the codebase and reducing duplicate implementation.

### Success Criteria
- A single, reusable slugify function is available in the utility module
- All edge cases (spaces, underscores, special characters, repeated hyphens) are handled correctly
- Function behavior matches the specified transformation rules exactly
- The implementation is testable and maintainable

## Functional Requirements

### REQ-001: Text Normalization [Must Have]
**User**: Developer using the utility module
**Need**: Convert arbitrary text strings into normalized lowercase format
**Rationale**: URLs and identifiers should be case-insensitive and follow lowercase convention for consistency and compatibility

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- All uppercase letters (A-Z) are converted to lowercase (a-z)
- Mixed-case input produces consistent lowercase output
- Non-ASCII letters retain their character but follow lowercase transformation if applicable

**Examples**:
- Input: `"Hello"` → Output: `"hello"`
- Input: `"WORLD"` → Output: `"world"`
- Input: `"MixedCase"` → Output: `"mixedcase"`

---

### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement [Must Have]
**User**: Developer using the utility module
**Need**: Replace spaces and underscores with hyphens
**Rationale**: Hyphens are the standard word separator in URLs and improve readability while maintaining URL safety

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- All space characters (` `) are replaced with hyphens (`-`)
- All underscore characters (`_`) are replaced with hyphens (`-`)
- Multiple consecutive spaces/underscores are handled by the hyphen collapse rule (REQ-004)

**Examples**:
- Input: `"hello world"` → Output: `"hello-world"`
- Input: `"foo_bar"` → Output: `"foo-bar"`
- Input: `"one two three"` → Output: `"one-two-three"`

---

### REQ-003: Special Character Removal [Must Have]
**User**: Developer using the utility module
**Need**: Remove characters that are not letters, numbers, or hyphens
**Rationale**: URLs and identifiers should only contain safe, alphanumeric characters plus hyphens to avoid encoding issues and ensure universal compatibility

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Only alphanumeric characters (a-z, 0-9) and hyphens (`-`) are retained in the output
- Punctuation marks (`!`, `?`, `.`, `,`, `;`, `:`, `'`, `"`, etc.) are removed
- Special symbols (`@`, `#`, `$`, `%`, `&`, `*`, `(`, `)`, etc.) are removed
- Characters are removed (not replaced), allowing adjacent characters to be handled by collapse/trim rules

**Examples**:
- Input: `"Hello, World!"` → Output: `"hello-world"`
- Input: `"user@example.com"` → Output: `"userexamplecom"`
- Input: `"Price: $99.99"` → Output: `"price-9999"`

---

### REQ-004: Hyphen Collapse [Must Have]
**User**: Developer using the utility module
**Need**: Consolidate multiple consecutive hyphens into a single hyphen
**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens reduce readability and create unnecessarily long slugs; single hyphens are cleaner and more professional

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Two or more consecutive hyphens are replaced with a single hyphen
- This applies after space/underscore replacement and special character removal
- Single hyphens remain unchanged

**Examples**:
- Input: `"a---b"` → Output: `"a-b"`
- Input: `"foo--bar"` → Output: `"foo-bar"`
- Input: `"multiple   spaces"` (becomes `"multiple---spaces"` after replacement) → Output: `"multiple-spaces"`

---

### REQ-005: Leading and Trailing Hyphen Removal [Must Have]
**User**: Developer using the utility module
**Need**: Remove hyphens from the beginning and end of the slug
**Rationale**: Slugs should start and end with meaningful content (letters or numbers), not separators, for cleaner appearance and better usability

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Any hyphens at the start of the string are removed
- Any hyphens at the end of the string are removed
- Interior hyphens are preserved
- Empty or whitespace-only input may result in an empty string after processing

**Examples**:
- Input: `"-hello-"` → Output: `"hello"`
- Input: `"--start"` → Output: `"start"`
- Input: `"end--"` → Output: `"end"`
- Input: `" --- "` → Output: `""`

---

### REQ-006: Transformation Order [Must Have]
**User**: Developer using the utility module
**Need**: Apply transformations in the correct sequence to achieve expected results
**Rationale**: The order of operations affects the final output; a defined sequence ensures predictable behavior

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Transformations are applied in this order:
  1. Convert to lowercase
  2. Replace spaces and underscores with hyphens
  3. Remove non-alphanumeric characters (except hyphens)
  4. Collapse repeated hyphens
  5. Trim leading and trailing hyphens
- The function produces correct output for all provided examples

**Examples** (complete transformation):
- Input: `"Hello, World!"` → `"hello, world!"` → `"hello,-world!"` → `"hello-world"` → `"hello-world"` → `"hello-world"`
- Input: `"Foo__Bar"` → `"foo__bar"` → `"foo--bar"` → `"foo--bar"` → `"foo-bar"` → `"foo-bar"`
- Input: `" a---b "` → `" a---b "` → `"--a---b--"` → `"--a---b--"` → `"-a-b-"` → `"a-b"`

## User Stories

### STORY-001: Generate URL Slug from Title
**As a** developer building a content management feature
**I want** to convert article titles into URL-safe slugs
**So that** I can create clean, readable URLs for published content

**Acceptance Scenarios**:
```gherkin
GIVEN I have an article title "Hello, World!"
WHEN I call slugify("Hello, World!")
THEN I receive "hello-world"

GIVEN I have a title with underscores "Foo__Bar"
WHEN I call slugify("Foo__Bar")
THEN I receive "foo-bar"

GIVEN I have a title with multiple hyphens "a---b"
WHEN I call slugify("a---b")
THEN I receive "a-b"
```

---

### STORY-002: Handle Edge Cases Gracefully
**As a** developer using the slugify utility
**I want** the function to handle edge cases without errors
**So that** I can rely on it for any text input without special error handling

**Acceptance Scenarios**:
```gherkin
GIVEN I have empty input ""
WHEN I call slugify("")
THEN I receive ""

GIVEN I have whitespace-only input "   "
WHEN I call slugify("   ")
THEN I receive ""

# Design: Slugify Utility

**Feature ID**: slugify-utility
**Version**: 1.0.0
**Status**: Draft
**Created**: 2026-07-28

## Summary

Add a pure `slugify` function to the existing utils module that transforms arbitrary text into URL-safe slugs using a defined sequence of transformations: lowercase conversion, space/underscore replacement with hyphens, special character removal, hyphen collapse, and leading/trailing hyphen trim. This approach leverages standard JavaScript string methods with regex patterns, requiring no external dependencies and maintaining consistency with the existing utility module structure.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Input["Input String"] --> T1["1. toLowerCase()"]
    T1 --> T2["2. Replace spaces/underscores with hyphens"]
    T2 --> T3["3. Remove non-alphanumeric (except hyphens)"]
    T3 --> T4["4. Collapse multiple hyphens"]
    T4 --> T5["5. Trim leading/trailing hyphens"]
    T5 --> Output["Slug Output"]
```

## Contracts

| Contract | Producer | Consumer | Required Fields Or Outputs |
|----------|----------|----------|----------------------------|
| slugify function signature | utils.ts | Any importing module | `(text: string): string` |
| Transformation rules | slugify | Tests | Lowercase, hyphen-separated, alphanumeric-only output |

## Component Plan

| # | Component | Description | Files Changed |
|---|-----------|-------------|---------------|
| T1 | slugify function | Pure function implementing text-to-slug transformation following REQ-001 through REQ-006 | `src/utils.ts` |
| T2 | slugify tests | Comprehensive unit tests covering all requirements and validation examples | `src/utils.test.ts` |

## Implementation DAG

**Parallel Groups** (tasks with no inter-dependencies):

1. [T1] - Implementation can be written standalone

**Dependencies**:

- T2 -> T1 (Interface: tests import and call slugify function from utils.ts)

**Critical Path**: T1 -> T2

## Validation Plan

| Behavior Or Contract | Failure Mode Covered | Test Type | Evidence Or Command |
|----------------------|----------------------|-----------|---------------------|
| Lowercase conversion (REQ-001) | Mixed case not normalized | unit | `bun test` - verify "Hello" -> "hello" |
| Space/underscore replacement (REQ-002) | Separators not converted | unit | `bun test` - verify "hello world", "foo_bar" |
| Special char removal (REQ-003) | Invalid chars in output | unit | `bun test` - verify "Hello, World!" -> "hello-world" |
| Hyphen collapse (REQ-004) | Multiple hyphens remain | unit | `bun test` - verify "a---b" -> "a-b" |
| Leading/trailing trim (REQ-005) | Edge hyphens remain | unit | `bun test` - verify "-hello-" -> "hello" |
| Transformation order (REQ-006) | Incorrect sequence produces wrong output | unit | `bun test` - verify all validation examples |
| Empty/edge input handling | Error or unexpected output | unit | `bun test` - verify "", "   ", "!@#$%" -> "" |
| Function signature | Type errors | unit | TypeScript compilation succeeds |

## Documentation Impact

| Type | Target | Section | KB Source | Rationale |
|------|--------|---------|-----------|-----------|
| edit | modules.md | Utils | index.md:modules | Add slugify to documented utility functions |

## Open Risks

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|--------|------------|
| Regex edge cases with unusual Unicode input | LOW | Requirements explicitly scope to ASCII alphanumeric; tests cover all specified examples |
| Performance degradation on very long strings | LOW | NFR-001 specifies typical input <500 chars; standard string methods are optimized |

# Design Decisions: Slugify Utility

**Feature ID**: slugify-utility
**Created**: 2026-07-28

## Decision Log

| ID | Decision | Choice | Rationale | Alternatives Considered |
|----|----------|--------|-----------|------------------------|
| D1 | Implementation approach | Chained regex replacements | Standard JavaScript string methods are sufficient for all requirements; no external library needed | External library (slugify, speakingurl) - rejected due to no-dependencies constraint |
| D2 | Character set handling | ASCII alphanumeric only (a-z, 0-9) | Requirements explicitly scope to ASCII; Unicode normalization out of scope | Unicode-aware regex with normalize() - rejected as out of scope |
| D3 | Test structure | Add to existing utils.test.ts | Follow project pattern of co-located tests; maintain single test file for utils | Separate slugify.test.ts - rejected to maintain existing pattern |
| D4 | Function location | Add to existing src/utils.ts | Requirements constraint specifies adding to existing utility module | New module src/slugify.ts - rejected per requirements |
| D5 | Empty input handling | Return empty string | Conservative default aligns with transformation rules; no error thrown for edge cases | Throw error on empty - rejected as overly strict for utility function |

---

## AFK Mode: Auto-Selected Technology Decisions

| Decision | Choice | Source | Rationale |
|----------|--------|--------|-----------|
| Implementation language | TypeScript | Requirements constraint | Requirements explicitly specify TypeScript implementation |
| Test framework | Bun test runner | patterns.md, existing codebase | Project uses Bun's built-in test runner with describe/test/expect pattern |
| String manipulation approach | Native JavaScript regex | patterns.md | No external dependencies policy; standard methods sufficient |
| Function naming convention | camelCase (slugify) | patterns.md | Project pattern specifies camelCase for functions |
| Documentation style | JSDoc comments | Existing utils.ts | Follow existing function documentation pattern |

    25→## Functional Requirements
    26→
    27→### REQ-001: Text Normalization [Must Have]
    28→**User**: Developer using the utility module

    30→**Rationale**: URLs and identifiers should be case-insensitive and follow lowercase convention for consistency and compatibility

    43→
    44→### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement [Must Have]
    45→**User**: Developer using the utility module

    55→- Input: `"hello world"` → Output: `"hello-world"`
    56→- Input: `"foo_bar"` → Output: `"foo-bar"`
    57→- Input: `"one two three"` → Output: `"one-two-three"`
    58→
    59→---
    60→
    61→### REQ-003: Special Character Removal [Must Have]
    62→**User**: Developer using the utility module
    63→**Need**: Remove characters that are not letters, numbers, or hyphens
    64→**Rationale**: URLs and identifiers should only contain safe, alphanumeric characters plus hyphens to avoid encoding issues and ensure universal compatibility
    65→
    66→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    67→- Only alphanumeric characters (a-z, 0-9) and hyphens (`-`) are retained in the output
    68→- Punctuation marks (`!`, `?`, `.`, `,`, `;`, `:`, `'`, `"`, etc.) are removed
    69→- Special symbols (`@`, `#`, `$`, `%`, `&`, `*`, `(`, `)`, etc.) are removed
    70→- Characters are removed (not replaced), allowing adjacent characters to be handled by collapse/trim rules
    71→
    72→**Examples**:
    73→- Input: `"Hello, World!"` → Output: `"hello-world"`
    74→- Input: `"user@example.com"` → Output: `"userexamplecom"`
    75→- Input: `"Price: $99.99"` → Output: `"price-9999"`
    76→
    77→---
    78→
    79→### REQ-004: Hyphen Collapse [Must Have]
    80→**User**: Developer using the utility module
    81→**Need**: Consolidate multiple consecutive hyphens into a single hyphen
    82→**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens reduce readability and create unnecessarily long slugs; single hyphens are cleaner and more professional
    83→
    84→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    85→- Two or more consecutive hyphens are replaced with a single hyphen
    86→- This applies after space/underscore replacement and special character removal
    87→- Single hyphens remain unchanged
    88→
    89→**Examples**:
    90→- Input: `"a---b"` → Output: `"a-b"`
    91→- Input: `"foo--bar"` → Output: `"foo-bar"`
    92→- Input: `"multiple   spaces"` (becomes `"multiple---spaces"` after replacement) → Output: `"multiple-spaces"`
    93→
    94→---
    95→
    96→### REQ-005: Leading and Trailing Hyphen Removal [Must Have]
    97→**User**: Developer using the utility module
    98→**Need**: Remove hyphens from the beginning and end of the slug
    99→**Rationale**: Slugs should start and end with meaningful content (letters or numbers), not separators, for cleaner appearance and better usability
   100→
   101→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   102→- Any hyphens at the start of the string are removed
   103→- Any hyphens at the end of the string are removed
   104→- Interior hyphens are preserved
   105→- Empty or whitespace-only input may result in an empty string after processing
   106→
   107→**Examples**:
   108→- Input: `"-hello-"` → Output: `"hello"`
   109→- Input: `"--start"` → Output: `"start"`
   110→- Input: `"end--"` → Output: `"end"`
   111→- Input: `" --- "` → Output: `""`
   112→
   113→---
   114→
   115→### REQ-006: Transformation Order [Must Have]
   116→**User**: Developer using the utility module
   117→**Need**: Apply transformations in the correct sequence to achieve expected results
   118→**Rationale**: The order of operations affects the final output; a defined sequence ensures predictable behavior
   119→

   121→- Transformations are applied in this order:
   122→  1. Convert to lowercase
   123→  2. Replace spaces and underscores with hyphens
   124→  3. Remove non-alphanumeric characters (except hyphens)
   125→  4. Collapse repeated hyphens
   126→  5. Trim leading and trailing hyphens
   127→- The function produces correct output for all provided examples
   128→
   129→**Examples** (complete transformation):
   130→- Input: `"Hello, World!"` → `"hello, world!"` → `"hello,-world!"` → `"hello-world"` → `"hello-world"` → `"hello-world"`
   131→- Input: `"Foo__Bar"` → `"foo__bar"` → `"foo--bar"` → `"foo--bar"` → `"foo-bar"` → `"foo-bar"`
   132→- Input: `" a---b "` → `" a---b "` → `"--a---b--"` → `"--a---b--"` → `"-a-b-"` → `"a-b"`

   135→
   136→### STORY-001: Generate URL Slug from Title

   146→

   148→WHEN I call slugify("Foo__Bar")
   149→THEN I receive "foo-bar"
   150→
   151→GIVEN I have a title with multiple hyphens "a---b"
   152→WHEN I call slugify("a---b")
   153→THEN I receive "a-b"
   154→```
   155→
   156→---

   158→### STORY-002: Handle Edge Cases Gracefully

   186→**Rationale**: String utility functions are often called frequently; reasonable performance prevents bottlenecks

     9→# Feature Requirements: slugify-utility
    10→
    11→## Overview
    12→
    13→### Purpose
    14→Provide a string utility function that converts arbitrary text into URL-safe, human-readable slugs suitable for use in web addresses, file names, and identifiers.
    15→
    16→### Business Context
    17→Slugs are essential for creating clean, SEO-friendly URLs and consistent identifiers across the application. This utility will standardize text transformation logic, ensuring consistent slug generation throughout the codebase and reducing duplicate implementation.
    18→
    19→### Success Criteria
    20→- A single, reusable slugify function is available in the utility module
    21→- All edge cases (spaces, underscores, special characters, repeated hyphens) are handled correctly
    22→- Function behavior matches the specified transformation rules exactly
    23→- The implementation is testable and maintainable
    24→
    25→## Functional Requirements
    26→
    27→### REQ-001: Text Normalization [Must Have]
    28→**User**: Developer using the utility module
    29→**Need**: Convert arbitrary text strings into normalized lowercase format
    30→**Rationale**: URLs and identifiers should be case-insensitive and follow lowercase convention for consistency and compatibility
    31→
    32→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    33→- All uppercase letters (A-Z) are converted to lowercase (a-z)
    34→- Mixed-case input produces consistent lowercase output
    35→- Non-ASCII letters retain their character but follow lowercase transformation if applicable
    36→
    37→**Examples**:
    38→- Input: `"Hello"` → Output: `"hello"`
    39→- Input: `"WORLD"` → Output: `"world"`
    40→- Input: `"MixedCase"` → Output: `"mixedcase"`
    41→
    42→---
    43→
    44→### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement [Must Have]
    45→**User**: Developer using the utility module
    46→**Need**: Replace spaces and underscores with hyphens
    47→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the standard word separator in URLs and improve readability while maintaining URL safety
    48→
    49→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    50→- All space characters (` `) are replaced with hyphens (`-`)
    51→- All underscore characters (`_`) are replaced with hyphens (`-`)
    52→- Multiple consecutive spaces/underscores are handled by the hyphen collapse rule (REQ-004)
    53→
    54→**Examples**:
    55→- Input: `"hello world"` → Output: `"hello-world"`
    56→- Input: `"foo_bar"` → Output: `"foo-bar"`
    57→- Input: `"one two three"` → Output: `"one-two-three"`
    58→
    59→---
    60→
    61→### REQ-003: Special Character Removal [Must Have]
    62→**User**: Developer using the utility module
    63→**Need**: Remove characters that are not letters, numbers, or hyphens
    64→**Rationale**: URLs and identifiers should only contain safe, alphanumeric characters plus hyphens to avoid encoding issues and ensure universal compatibility
    65→
    66→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    67→- Only alphanumeric characters (a-z, 0-9) and hyphens (`-`) are retained in the output
    68→- Punctuation marks (`!`, `?`, `.`, `,`, `;`, `:`, `'`, `"`, etc.) are removed
    69→- Special symbols (`@`, `#`, `$`, `%`, `&`, `*`, `(`, `)`, etc.) are removed
    70→- Characters are removed (not replaced), allowing adjacent characters to be handled by collapse/trim rules
    71→
    72→**Examples**:
    73→- Input: `"Hello, World!"` → Output: `"hello-world"`
    74→- Input: `"user@example.com"` → Output: `"userexamplecom"`
    75→- Input: `"Price: $99.99"` → Output: `"price-9999"`
    76→
    77→---
    78→
    79→### REQ-004: Hyphen Collapse [Must Have]
    80→**User**: Developer using the utility module
    81→**Need**: Consolidate multiple consecutive hyphens into a single hyphen
    82→**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens reduce readability and create unnecessarily long slugs; single hyphens are cleaner and more professional
    83→
    84→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    85→- Two or more consecutive hyphens are replaced with a single hyphen
    86→- This applies after space/underscore replacement and special character removal
    87→- Single hyphens remain unchanged
    88→
    89→**Examples**:
    90→- Input: `"a---b"` → Output: `"a-b"`
    91→- Input: `"foo--bar"` → Output: `"foo-bar"`
    92→- Input: `"multiple   spaces"` (becomes `"multiple---spaces"` after replacement) → Output: `"multiple-spaces"`
    93→
    94→---
    95→
    96→### REQ-005: Leading and Trailing Hyphen Removal [Must Have]
    97→**User**: Developer using the utility module
    98→**Need**: Remove hyphens from the beginning and end of the slug
    99→**Rationale**: Slugs should start and end with meaningful content (letters or numbers), not separators, for cleaner appearance and better usability
   100→
   101→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   102→- Any hyphens at the start of the string are removed
   103→- Any hyphens at the end of the string are removed
   104→- Interior hyphens are preserved
   105→- Empty or whitespace-only input may result in an empty string after processing
   106→
   107→**Examples**:
   108→- Input: `"-hello-"` → Output: `"hello"`
   109→- Input: `"--start"` → Output: `"start"`
   110→- Input: `"end--"` → Output: `"end"`
   111→- Input: `" --- "` → Output: `""`
   112→
   113→---
   114→
   115→### REQ-006: Transformation Order [Must Have]
   116→**User**: Developer using the utility module
   117→**Need**: Apply transformations in the correct sequence to achieve expected results
   118→**Rationale**: The order of operations affects the final output; a defined sequence ensures predictable behavior
   119→
   120→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   121→- Transformations are applied in this order:
   122→  1. Convert to lowercase
   123→  2. Replace spaces and underscores with hyphens
   124→  3. Remove non-alphanumeric characters (except hyphens)
   125→  4. Collapse repeated hyphens
   126→  5. Trim leading and trailing hyphens
   127→- The function produces correct output for all provided examples
   128→
   129→**Examples** (complete transformation):
   130→- Input: `"Hello, World!"` → `"hello, world!"` → `"hello,-world!"` → `"hello-world"` → `"hello-world"` → `"hello-world"`
   131→- Input: `"Foo__Bar"` → `"foo__bar"` → `"foo--bar"` → `"foo--bar"` → `"foo-bar"` → `"foo-bar"`
   132→- Input: `" a---b "` → `" a---b "` → `"--a---b--"` → `"--a---b--"` → `"-a-b-"` → `"a-b"`
   133→
   134→## User Stories
   135→
   136→### STORY-001: Generate URL Slug from Title
   137→**As a** developer building a content management feature
   138→**I want** to convert article titles into URL-safe slugs
   139→**So that** I can create clean, readable URLs for published content
   140→
   141→**Acceptance Scenarios**:
   142→```gherkin
   143→GIVEN I have an article title "Hello, World!"
   144→WHEN I call slugify("Hello, World!")
   145→THEN I receive "hello-world"
   146→
   147→GIVEN I have a title with underscores "Foo__Bar"
   148→WHEN I call slugify("Foo__Bar")
   149→THEN I receive "foo-bar"
   150→
   151→GIVEN I have a title with multiple hyphens "a---b"
   152→WHEN I call slugify("a---b")
   153→THEN I receive "a-b"
   154→```
   155→
   156→---
   157→
   158→### STORY-002: Handle Edge Cases Gracefully
   159→**As a** developer using the slugify utility
   160→**I want** the function to handle edge cases without errors
   161→**So that** I can rely on it for any text input without special error handling
   162→
   163→**Acceptance Scenarios**:
   164→```gherkin
   165→GIVEN I have empty input ""
   166→WHEN I call slugify("")
   167→THEN I receive ""
   168→
   169→GIVEN I have whitespace-only input "   "
   170→WHEN I call slugify("   ")
   171→THEN I receive ""
   172→
   173→GIVEN I have special characters only "!@#$%"
   174→WHEN I call slugify("!@#$%")
   175→THEN I receive ""
   176→
   177→GIVEN I have leading/trailing spaces "  hello  "
   178→WHEN I call slugify("  hello  ")
   179→THEN I receive "hello"
   180→```
   181→
   182→## Non-Functional Requirements
   183→
   184→### NFR-001: Performance [Should Have]
   185→**Requirement**: The slugify function should process typical input strings (< 500 characters) in under 10ms
   186→**Rationale**: String utility functions are often called frequently; reasonable performance prevents bottlenecks
   187→**Acceptance**: Benchmark tests confirm processing time meets threshold for typical use cases
   188→
   189→### NFR-002: Testability [Must Have]
   190→**Requirement**: The function must be pure (no side effects) and easily testable with the provided examples
   191→**Rationale**: Pure functions are easier to test, debug, and maintain
   192→**Acceptance**: Unit tests can verify all requirements and examples without mocking or complex setup
   193→
   194→### NFR-003: Code Quality [Should Have]
   195→**Requirement**: Implementation should follow project TypeScript conventions and be maintainable
   196→**Rationale**: Consistent code quality supports long-term maintainability
   197→**Acceptance**: Code passes linting, follows naming conventions, and includes appropriate type annotations
   198→
   199→## Constraints
   200→
   201→### Technical Constraints
   202→- Implementation must be in TypeScript
   203→- Function must be added to the existing `src/utils.ts` module
   204→- Must be compatible with Bun runtime
   205→- Must not introduce external dependencies
   206→
   207→### Business Constraints
   208→- Must handle all provided examples correctly
   209→- Must be a pure function with no side effects
   210→- Must be backward-compatible with existing utility module structure
   211→
   212→## Dependencies
   213→
   214→### Internal Dependencies
   215→- Utility module (`src/utils.ts`) must exist and be extensible
   216→- Test infrastructure (`bun test`) must be available for validation
   217→
   218→### External Dependencies
   219→- None required (standard JavaScript string methods are sufficient)
   220→
   221→## Out of Scope
   222→
   223→The following are explicitly excluded from this feature:
   224→
   225→- **Custom separator configuration**: The hyphen is the fixed separator; no option to use underscores or other characters
   226→- **Unicode normalization**: Advanced Unicode handling (e.g., converting accented characters to ASCII equivalents) is not required
   227→- **Maximum length enforcement**: No truncation or length limiting
   228→- **Uniqueness guarantees**: The function does not ensure globally unique slugs or handle collisions
   229→- **Internationalization**: No locale-specific transformations or right-to-left text support
   230→- **Database integration**: No automatic slug persistence or collision detection
   231→- **URL encoding**: The function produces clean slugs but does not perform percent-encoding
   232→
   233→## Validation Examples
   234→
   235→These examples must pass validation testing:
   236→
   237→| Input | Expected Output | Rule Tested |
   238→|-------|----------------|-------------|
   239→| `"Hello, World!"` | `"hello-world"` | Lowercase + special char removal |
   240→| `"Foo__Bar"` | `"foo-bar"` | Underscore replacement + collapse |
   241→| `"a---b"` | `"a-b"` | Hyphen collapse |
   242→| `"  Hello  "` | `"hello"` | Trim + whitespace handling |
   243→| `"UPPERCASE"` | `"uppercase"` | Lowercase conversion |
   244→| `"123-456"` | `"123-456"` | Numbers and hyphens preserved |
   245→| `"!@#$%"` | `""` | Special chars only → empty |
   246→| `""` | `""` | Empty input → empty output |
   247→| `"one two three"` | `"one-two-three"` | Multiple space replacement |
   248→| `"-start-end-"` | `"start-end"` | Leading/trailing hyphen trim |
   249→
   250→## AFK Mode Decisions
   251→
   252→This requirements document was generated in AFK (away-from-keyboard) mode. The following decisions were made automatically:
   253→
   254→### Decision 1: PRD Association
   255→**Point**: PRD selection
   256→**Choice**: No PRD associated
   257→**Rationale**: No PRDs found in `.rp1/work/prds/` directory; this appears to be a standalone utility feature
   258→
   259→### Decision 2: Scope Definition
   260→**Point**: URL encoding vs. slug generation
   261→**Choice**: Focus on slug generation only (no percent-encoding)
   262→**Rationale**: Input specification focuses on character transformation rules, not URL encoding; slug generation is the core need
   263→
   264→### Decision 3: Empty String Handling
   265→**Point**: Behavior for empty or invalid input
   266→**Choice**: Return empty string for inputs that become empty after transformation
   267→**Rationale**: Conservative default aligns with transformation rules (trim all hyphens → empty result for separator-only input)
   268→
   269→### Decision 4: Character Set
   270→**Point**: Definition of "letter" and "number"
   271→**Choice**: Alphanumeric refers to a-z and 0-9 (ASCII only)
   272→**Rationale**: Input examples use ASCII characters; no Unicode or internationalization requirements specified
   273→
   274→### Decision 5: Function Signature
   275→**Point**: Input parameter types and return type
   276→**Choice**: Single string parameter, returns string
   277→**Rationale**: All examples show simple text transformation with no additional configuration or options
   278→
   279→## Acceptance Checklist
   280→
   281→Before marking this feature as complete, verify:
   282→
   283→- [ ] All validation examples produce expected output
   284→- [ ] Function is exported from `src/utils.ts`
   285→- [ ] Unit tests cover all requirements (REQ-001 through REQ-006)
   286→- [ ] Unit tests include all validation examples
   287→- [ ] Edge cases (empty, whitespace-only, special chars only) are tested
   288→- [ ] Function signature accepts string and returns string
   289→- [ ] TypeScript type annotations are present

# Feature Requirements: slugify-utility

## Overview

### Purpose
Provide a string utility function that converts arbitrary text into URL-safe, human-readable slugs suitable for use in web addresses, file names, and identifiers.

### Business Context
Slugs are essential for creating clean, SEO-friendly URLs and consistent identifiers across the application. This utility will standardize text transformation logic, ensuring consistent slug generation throughout the codebase and reducing duplicate implementation.

### Success Criteria
- A single, reusable slugify function is available in the utility module
- All edge cases (spaces, underscores, special characters, repeated hyphens) are handled correctly
- Function behavior matches the specified transformation rules exactly
- The implementation is testable and maintainable

## Functional Requirements

### REQ-001: Text Normalization [Must Have]
**User**: Developer using the utility module
**Need**: Convert arbitrary text strings into normalized lowercase format
**Rationale**: URLs and identifiers should be case-insensitive and follow lowercase convention for consistency and compatibility

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- All uppercase letters (A-Z) are converted to lowercase (a-z)
- Mixed-case input produces consistent lowercase output
- Non-ASCII letters retain their character but follow lowercase transformation if applicable

**Examples**:
- Input: `"Hello"` → Output: `"hello"`
- Input: `"WORLD"` → Output: `"world"`
- Input: `"MixedCase"` → Output: `"mixedcase"`

---

### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement [Must Have]
**User**: Developer using the utility module
**Need**: Replace spaces and underscores with hyphens
**Rationale**: Hyphens are the standard word separator in URLs and improve readability while maintaining URL safety

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- All space characters (` `) are replaced with hyphens (`-`)
- All underscore characters (`_`) are replaced with hyphens (`-`)
- Multiple consecutive spaces/underscores are handled by the hyphen collapse rule (REQ-004)

**Examples**:
- Input: `"hello world"` → Output: `"hello-world"`
- Input: `"foo_bar"` → Output: `"foo-bar"`
- Input: `"one two three"` → Output: `"one-two-three"`

---

### REQ-003: Special Character Removal [Must Have]
**User**: Developer using the utility module
**Need**: Remove characters that are not letters, numbers, or hyphens
**Rationale**: URLs and identifiers should only contain safe, alphanumeric characters plus hyphens to avoid encoding issues and ensure universal compatibility

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Only alphanumeric characters (a-z, 0-9) and hyphens (`-`) are retained in the output
- Punctuation marks (`!`, `?`, `.`, `,`, `;`, `:`, `'`, `"`, etc.) are removed
- Special symbols (`@`, `#`, `$`, `%`, `&`, `*`, `(`, `)`, etc.) are removed
- Characters are removed (not replaced), allowing adjacent characters to be handled by collapse/trim rules

**Examples**:
- Input: `"Hello, World!"` → Output: `"hello-world"`
- Input: `"user@example.com"` → Output: `"userexamplecom"`
- Input: `"Price: $99.99"` → Output: `"price-9999"`

---

### REQ-004: Hyphen Collapse [Must Have]
**User**: Developer using the utility module
**Need**: Consolidate multiple consecutive hyphens into a single hyphen
**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens reduce readability and create unnecessarily long slugs; single hyphens are cleaner and more professional

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Two or more consecutive hyphens are replaced with a single hyphen
- This applies after space/underscore replacement and special character removal
- Single hyphens remain unchanged

**Examples**:
- Input: `"a---b"` → Output: `"a-b"`
- Input: `"foo--bar"` → Output: `"foo-bar"`
- Input: `"multiple   spaces"` (becomes `"multiple---spaces"` after replacement) → Output: `"multiple-spaces"`

---

### REQ-005: Leading and Trailing Hyphen Removal [Must Have]
**User**: Developer using the utility module
**Need**: Remove hyphens from the beginning and end of the slug
**Rationale**: Slugs should start and end with meaningful content (letters or numbers), not separators, for cleaner appearance and better usability

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Any hyphens at the start of the string are removed
- Any hyphens at the end of the string are removed
- Interior hyphens are preserved
- Empty or whitespace-only input may result in an empty string after processing

**Examples**:
- Input: `"-hello-"` → Output: `"hello"`
- Input: `"--start"` → Output: `"start"`
- Input: `"end--"` → Output: `"end"`
- Input: `" --- "` → Output: `""`

---

### REQ-006: Transformation Order [Must Have]
**User**: Developer using the utility module
**Need**: Apply transformations in the correct sequence to achieve expected results
**Rationale**: The order of operations affects the final output; a defined sequence ensures predictable behavior

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Transformations are applied in this order:
  1. Convert to lowercase
  2. Replace spaces and underscores with hyphens
  3. Remove non-alphanumeric characters (except hyphens)
  4. Collapse repeated hyphens
  5. Trim leading and trailing hyphens
- The function produces correct output for all provided examples

**Examples** (complete transformation):
- Input: `"Hello, World!"` → `"hello, world!"` → `"hello,-world!"` → `"hello-world"` → `"hello-world"` → `"hello-world"`
- Input: `"Foo__Bar"` → `"foo__bar"` → `"foo--bar"` → `"foo--bar"` → `"foo-bar"` → `"foo-bar"`
- Input: `" a---b "` → `" a---b "` → `"--a---b--"` → `"--a---b--"` → `"-a-b-"` → `"a-b"`

## User Stories

### STORY-001: Generate URL Slug from Title
**As a** developer building a content management feature
**I want** to convert article titles into URL-safe slugs
**So that** I can create clean, readable URLs for published content

**Acceptance Scenarios**:
```gherkin
GIVEN I have an article title "Hello, World!"
WHEN I call slugify("Hello, World!")
THEN I receive "hello-world"

GIVEN I have a title with underscores "Foo__Bar"
WHEN I call slugify("Foo__Bar")
THEN I receive "foo-bar"

GIVEN I have a title with multiple hyphens "a---b"
WHEN I call slugify("a---b")
THEN I receive "a-b"
```

---

### STORY-002: Handle Edge Cases Gracefully
**As a** developer using the slugify utility
**I want** the function to handle edge cases without errors
**So that** I can rely on it for any text input without special error handling

**Acceptance Scenarios**:
```gherkin
GIVEN I have empty input ""
WHEN I call slugify("")
THEN I receive ""

GIVEN I have whitespace-only input "   "
WHEN I call slugify("   ")
THEN I receive ""

GIVEN I have special characters only "!@#$%"
WHEN I call slugify("!@#$%")
THEN I receive ""

GIVEN I have leading/trailing spaces "  hello  "
WHEN I call slugify("  hello  ")
THEN I receive "hello"
```

## Non-Functional Requirements

### NFR-001: Performance [Should Have]
**Requirement**: The slugify function should process typical input strings (< 500 characters) in under 10ms
**Rationale**: String utility functions are often called frequently; reasonable performance prevents bottlenecks
**Acceptance**: Benchmark tests confirm processing time meets threshold for typical use cases

### NFR-002: Testability [Must Have]
**Requirement**: The function must be pure (no side effects) and easily testable with the provided examples
**Rationale**: Pure functions are easier to test, debug, and maintain
**Acceptance**: Unit tests can verify all requirements and examples without mocking or complex setup

### NFR-003: Code Quality [Should Have]
**Requirement**: Implementation should follow project TypeScript conventions and be maintainable
**Rationale**: Consistent code quality supports long-term maintainability
**Acceptance**: Code passes linting, follows naming conventions, and includes appropriate type annotations

## Constraints

### Technical Constraints
- Implementation must be in TypeScript
- Function must be added to the existing `src/utils.ts` module
- Must be compatible with Bun runtime
- Must not introduce external dependencies

### Business Constraints
- Must handle all provided examples correctly
- Must be a pure function with no side effects
- Must be backward-compatible with existing utility module structure

## Dependencies

### Internal Dependencies
- Utility module (`src/utils.ts`) must exist and be extensible
- Test infrastructure (`bun test`) must be available for validation

### External Dependencies
- None required (standard JavaScript string methods are sufficient)

## Out of Scope

The following are explicitly excluded from this feature:

- **Custom separator configuration**: The hyphen is the fixed separator; no option to use underscores or other characters
- **Unicode normalization**: Advanced Unicode handling (e.g., converting accented characters to ASCII equivalents) is not required
- **Maximum length enforcement**: No truncation or length limiting
- **Uniqueness guarantees**: The function does not ensure globally unique slugs or handle collisions
- **Internationalization**: No locale-specific transformations or right-to-left text support
- **Database integration**: No automatic slug persistence or collision detection
- **URL encoding**: The function produces clean slugs but does not perform percent-encoding

## Validation Examples

These examples must pass validation testing:

| Input | Expected Output | Rule Tested |
|-------|----------------|-------------|
| `"Hello, World!"` | `"hello-world"` | Lowercase + special char removal |
| `"Foo__Bar"` | `"foo-bar"` | Underscore replacement + collapse |
| `"a---b"` | `"a-b"` | Hyphen collapse |
| `"  Hello  "` | `"hello"` | Trim + whitespace handling |
| `"UPPERCASE"` | `"uppercase"` | Lowercase conversion |
| `"123-456"` | `"123-456"` | Numbers and hyphens preserved |
| `"!@#$%"` | `""` | Special chars only → empty |
| `""` | `""` | Empty input → empty output |
| `"one two three"` | `"one-two-three"` | Multiple space replacement |
| `"-start-end-"` | `"start-end"` | Leading/trailing hyphen trim |

## AFK Mode Decisions

This requirements document was generated in AFK (away-from-keyboard) mode. The following decisions were made automatically:

### Decision 1: PRD Association
**Point**: PRD selection
**Choice**: No PRD associated
**Rationale**: No PRDs found in `.rp1/work/prds/` directory; this appears to be a standalone utility feature

### Decision 2: Scope Definition
**Point**: URL encoding vs. slug generation
**Choice**: Focus on slug generation only (no percent-encoding)
**Rationale**: Input specification focuses on character transformation rules, not URL encoding; slug generation is the core need

### Decision 3: Empty String Handling
**Point**: Behavior for empty or invalid input
**Choice**: Return empty string for inputs that become empty after transformation
**Rationale**: Conservative default aligns with transformation rules (trim all hyphens → empty result for separator-only input)

### Decision 4: Character Set
**Point**: Definition of "letter" and "number"
**Choice**: Alphanumeric refers to a-z and 0-9 (ASCII only)
**Rationale**: Input examples use ASCII characters; no Unicode or internationalization requirements specified

### Decision 5: Function Signature
**Point**: Input parameter types and return type
**Choice**: Single string parameter, returns string
**Rationale**: All examples show simple text transformation with no additional configuration or options

## Acceptance Checklist

Before marking this feature as complete, verify:

- [ ] All validation examples produce expected output
- [ ] Function is exported from `src/utils.ts`
- [ ] Unit tests cover all requirements (REQ-001 through REQ-006)
- [ ] Unit tests include all validation examples
- [ ] Edge cases (empty, whitespace-only, special chars only) are tested
- [ ] Function signature accepts string and returns string
- [ ] TypeScript type annotations are present
- [ ] No external dependencies introduced
- [ ] Bun test suite passes completely

# Design: Slugify Utility

**Feature ID**: slugify-utility
**Version**: 1.0.0
**Status**: Draft
**Created**: 2026-07-28

## Summary

Add a pure `slugify` function to the existing utils module that transforms arbitrary text into URL-safe slugs using a defined sequence of transformations: lowercase conversion, space/underscore replacement with hyphens, special character removal, hyphen collapse, and leading/trailing hyphen trim. This approach leverages standard JavaScript string methods with regex patterns, requiring no external dependencies and maintaining consistency with the existing utility module structure.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Input["Input String"] --> T1["1. toLowerCase()"]
    T1 --> T2["2. Replace spaces/underscores with hyphens"]
    T2 --> T3["3. Remove non-alphanumeric (except hyphens)"]
    T3 --> T4["4. Collapse multiple hyphens"]
    T4 --> T5["5. Trim leading/trailing hyphens"]
    T5 --> Output["Slug Output"]
```

## Contracts

| Contract | Producer | Consumer | Required Fields Or Outputs |
|----------|----------|----------|----------------------------|
| slugify function signature | utils.ts | Any importing module | `(text: string): string` |
| Transformation rules | slugify | Tests | Lowercase, hyphen-separated, alphanumeric-only output |

## Component Plan

| # | Component | Description | Files Changed |
|---|-----------|-------------|---------------|
| T1 | slugify function | Pure function implementing text-to-slug transformation following REQ-001 through REQ-006 | `src/utils.ts` |
| T2 | slugify tests | Comprehensive unit tests covering all requirements and validation examples | `src/utils.test.ts` |

## Implementation DAG

**Parallel Groups** (tasks with no inter-dependencies):

1. [T1] - Implementation can be written standalone

**Dependencies**:

- T2 -> T1 (Interface: tests import and call slugify function from utils.ts)

**Critical Path**: T1 -> T2

## Validation Plan

| Behavior Or Contract | Failure Mode Covered | Test Type | Evidence Or Command |
|----------------------|----------------------|-----------|---------------------|
| Lowercase conversion (REQ-001) | Mixed case not normalized | unit | `bun test` - verify "Hello" -> "hello" |
| Space/underscore replacement (REQ-002) | Separators not converted | unit | `bun test` - verify "hello world", "foo_bar" |
| Special char removal (REQ-003) | Invalid chars in output | unit | `bun test` - verify "Hello, World!" -> "hello-world" |
| Hyphen collapse (REQ-004) | Multiple hyphens remain | unit | `bun test` - verify "a---b" -> "a-b" |
| Leading/trailing trim (REQ-005) | Edge hyphens remain | unit | `bun test` - verify "-hello-" -> "hello" |
| Transformation order (REQ-006) | Incorrect sequence produces wrong output | unit | `bun test` - verify all validation examples |
| Empty/edge input handling | Error or unexpected output | unit | `bun test` - verify "", "   ", "!@#$%" -> "" |
| Function signature | Type errors | unit | TypeScript compilation succeeds |

## Documentation Impact

| Type | Target | Section | KB Source | Rationale |
|------|--------|---------|-----------|-----------|
| edit | modules.md | Utils | index.md:modules | Add slugify to documented utility functions |

## Open Risks

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|--------|------------|
| Regex edge cases with unusual Unicode input | LOW | Requirements explicitly scope to ASCII alphanumeric; tests cover all specified examples |
| Performance degradation on very long strings | LOW | NFR-001 specifies typical input <500 chars; standard string methods are optimized |

     9→# Feature Requirements: slugify-utility
    10→
    11→## Overview
    12→
    13→### Purpose
    14→Provide a string utility function that converts arbitrary text into URL-safe, human-readable slugs suitable for use in web addresses, file names, and identifiers.
    15→
    16→### Business Context
    17→Slugs are essential for creating clean, SEO-friendly URLs and consistent identifiers across the application. This utility will standardize text transformation logic, ensuring consistent slug generation throughout the codebase and reducing duplicate implementation.
    18→
    19→### Success Criteria
    20→- A single, reusable slugify function is available in the utility module
    21→- All edge cases (spaces, underscores, special characters, repeated hyphens) are handled correctly
    22→- Function behavior matches the specified transformation rules exactly
    23→- The implementation is testable and maintainable
    24→
    25→## Functional Requirements
    26→
    27→### REQ-001: Text Normalization [Must Have]
    28→**User**: Developer using the utility module
    29→**Need**: Convert arbitrary text strings into normalized lowercase format
    30→**Rationale**: URLs and identifiers should be case-insensitive and follow lowercase convention for consistency and compatibility
    31→
    32→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    33→- All uppercase letters (A-Z) are converted to lowercase (a-z)
    34→- Mixed-case input produces consistent lowercase output
    35→- Non-ASCII letters retain their character but follow lowercase transformation if applicable
    36→
    37→**Examples**:
    38→- Input: `"Hello"` → Output: `"hello"`
    39→- Input: `"WORLD"` → Output: `"world"`
    40→- Input: `"MixedCase"` → Output: `"mixedcase"`
    41→
    42→---
    43→
    44→### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement [Must Have]
    45→**User**: Developer using the utility module
    46→**Need**: Replace spaces and underscores with hyphens
    47→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the standard word separator in URLs and improve readability while maintaining URL safety
    48→
    49→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    50→- All space characters (` `) are replaced with hyphens (`-`)
    51→- All underscore characters (`_`) are replaced with hyphens (`-`)
    52→- Multiple consecutive spaces/underscores are handled by the hyphen collapse rule (REQ-004)
    53→
    54→**Examples**:
    55→- Input: `"hello world"` → Output: `"hello-world"`
    56→- Input: `"foo_bar"` → Output: `"foo-bar"`
    57→- Input: `"one two three"` → Output: `"one-two-three"`
    58→
    59→---
    60→
    61→### REQ-003: Special Character Removal [Must Have]
    62→**User**: Developer using the utility module
    63→**Need**: Remove characters that are not letters, numbers, or hyphens
    64→**Rationale**: URLs and identifiers should only contain safe, alphanumeric characters plus hyphens to avoid encoding issues and ensure universal compatibility
    65→
    66→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    67→- Only alphanumeric characters (a-z, 0-9) and hyphens (`-`) are retained in the output
    68→- Punctuation marks (`!`, `?`, `.`, `,`, `;`, `:`, `'`, `"`, etc.) are removed
    69→- Special symbols (`@`, `#`, `$`, `%`, `&`, `*`, `(`, `)`, etc.) are removed
    70→- Characters are removed (not replaced), allowing adjacent characters to be handled by collapse/trim rules
    71→
    72→**Examples**:
    73→- Input: `"Hello, World!"` → Output: `"hello-world"`
    74→- Input: `"user@example.com"` → Output: `"userexamplecom"`
    75→- Input: `"Price: $99.99"` → Output: `"price-9999"`
    76→
    77→---
    78→
    79→### REQ-004: Hyphen Collapse [Must Have]
    80→**User**: Developer using the utility module
    81→**Need**: Consolidate multiple consecutive hyphens into a single hyphen
    82→**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens reduce readability and create unnecessarily long slugs; single hyphens are cleaner and more professional
    83→
    84→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    85→- Two or more consecutive hyphens are replaced with a single hyphen
    86→- This applies after space/underscore replacement and special character removal
    87→- Single hyphens remain unchanged
    88→
    89→**Examples**:
    90→- Input: `"a---b"` → Output: `"a-b"`
    91→- Input: `"foo--bar"` → Output: `"foo-bar"`
    92→- Input: `"multiple   spaces"` (becomes `"multiple---spaces"` after replacement) → Output: `"multiple-spaces"`
    93→
    94→---
    95→
    96→### REQ-005: Leading and Trailing Hyphen Removal [Must Have]
    97→**User**: Developer using the utility module
    98→**Need**: Remove hyphens from the beginning and end of the slug
    99→**Rationale**: Slugs should start and end with meaningful content (letters or numbers), not separators, for cleaner appearance and better usability
   100→
   101→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   102→- Any hyphens at the start of the string are removed
   103→- Any hyphens at the end of the string are removed
   104→- Interior hyphens are preserved
   105→- Empty or whitespace-only input may result in an empty string after processing
   106→
   107→**Examples**:
   108→- Input: `"-hello-"` → Output: `"hello"`
   109→- Input: `"--start"` → Output: `"start"`
   110→- Input: `"end--"` → Output: `"end"`
   111→- Input: `" --- "` → Output: `""`
   112→
   113→---
   114→
   115→### REQ-006: Transformation Order [Must Have]
   116→**User**: Developer using the utility module
   117→**Need**: Apply transformations in the correct sequence to achieve expected results
   118→**Rationale**: The order of operations affects the final output; a defined sequence ensures predictable behavior
   119→
   120→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   121→- Transformations are applied in this order:
   122→  1. Convert to lowercase
   123→  2. Replace spaces and underscores with hyphens
   124→  3. Remove non-alphanumeric characters (except hyphens)
   125→  4. Collapse repeated hyphens
   126→  5. Trim leading and trailing hyphens
   127→- The function produces correct output for all provided examples
   128→

   130→- Input: `"Hello, World!"` → `"hello, world!"` → `"hello,-world!"` → `"hello-world"` → `"hello-world"` → `"hello-world"`
   131→- Input: `"Foo__Bar"` → `"foo__bar"` → `"foo--bar"` → `"foo--bar"` → `"foo-bar"` → `"foo-bar"`
   132→- Input: `" a---b "` → `" a---b "` → `"--a---b--"` → `"--a---b--"` → `"-a-b-"` → `"a-b"`
   133→
   134→## User Stories
   135→
   136→### STORY-001: Generate URL Slug from Title
   137→**As a** developer building a content management feature
   138→**I want** to convert article titles into URL-safe slugs
   139→**So that** I can create clean, readable URLs for published content
   140→
   141→**Acceptance Scenarios**:

   143→GIVEN I have an article title "Hello, World!"
   144→WHEN I call slugify("Hello, World!")
   145→THEN I receive "hello-world"
   146→
   147→GIVEN I have a title with underscores "Foo__Bar"
   148→WHEN I call slugify("Foo__Bar")
   149→THEN I receive "foo-bar"
   150→
   151→GIVEN I have a title with multiple hyphens "a---b"
   152→WHEN I call slugify("a---b")
   153→THEN I receive "a-b"
   154→```
   155→
   156→---
   157→
   158→### STORY-002: Handle Edge Cases Gracefully
   159→**As a** developer using the slugify utility
   160→**I want** the function to handle edge cases without errors
   161→**So that** I can rely on it for any text input without special error handling

   174→WHEN I call slugify("!@#$%")

   180→```

   185→**Requirement**: The slugify function should process typical input strings (< 500 characters) in under 10ms
   186→**Rationale**: String utility functions are often called frequently; reasonable performance prevents bottlenecks

   191→**Rationale**: Pure functions are easier to test, debug, and maintain

   204→- Must be compatible with Bun runtime
   205→- Must not introduce external dependencies

   207→### Business Constraints

     9→# Feature Requirements: slugify-utility
    10→
    11→## Overview
    12→
    13→### Purpose
    14→Provide a string utility function that converts arbitrary text into URL-safe, human-readable slugs suitable for use in web addresses, file names, and identifiers.
    15→
    16→### Business Context
    17→Slugs are essential for creating clean, SEO-friendly URLs and consistent identifiers across the application. This utility will standardize text transformation logic, ensuring consistent slug generation throughout the codebase and reducing duplicate implementation.
    18→
    19→### Success Criteria
    20→- A single, reusable slugify function is available in the utility module
    21→- All edge cases (spaces, underscores, special characters, repeated hyphens) are handled correctly
    22→- Function behavior matches the specified transformation rules exactly
    23→- The implementation is testable and maintainable
    24→
    25→## Functional Requirements
    26→
    27→### REQ-001: Text Normalization [Must Have]
    28→**User**: Developer using the utility module
    29→**Need**: Convert arbitrary text strings into normalized lowercase format
    30→**Rationale**: URLs and identifiers should be case-insensitive and follow lowercase convention for consistency and compatibility
    31→
    32→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    33→- All uppercase letters (A-Z) are converted to lowercase (a-z)
    34→- Mixed-case input produces consistent lowercase output
    35→- Non-ASCII letters retain their character but follow lowercase transformation if applicable
    36→
    37→**Examples**:
    38→- Input: `"Hello"` → Output: `"hello"`
    39→- Input: `"WORLD"` → Output: `"world"`
    40→- Input: `"MixedCase"` → Output: `"mixedcase"`
    41→
    42→---
    43→
    44→### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement [Must Have]
    45→**User**: Developer using the utility module
    46→**Need**: Replace spaces and underscores with hyphens
    47→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the standard word separator in URLs and improve readability while maintaining URL safety
    48→
    49→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    50→- All space characters (` `) are replaced with hyphens (`-`)
    51→- All underscore characters (`_`) are replaced with hyphens (`-`)
    52→- Multiple consecutive spaces/underscores are handled by the hyphen collapse rule (REQ-004)
    53→
    54→**Examples**:
    55→- Input: `"hello world"` → Output: `"hello-world"`
    56→- Input: `"foo_bar"` → Output: `"foo-bar"`
    57→- Input: `"one two three"` → Output: `"one-two-three"`
    58→
    59→---
    60→
    61→### REQ-003: Special Character Removal [Must Have]
    62→**User**: Developer using the utility module
    63→**Need**: Remove characters that are not letters, numbers, or hyphens
    64→**Rationale**: URLs and identifiers should only contain safe, alphanumeric characters plus hyphens to avoid encoding issues and ensure universal compatibility
    65→
    66→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    67→- Only alphanumeric characters (a-z, 0-9) and hyphens (`-`) are retained in the output
    68→- Punctuation marks (`!`, `?`, `.`, `,`, `;`, `:`, `'`, `"`, etc.) are removed
    69→- Special symbols (`@`, `#`, `$`, `%`, `&`, `*`, `(`, `)`, etc.) are removed
    70→- Characters are removed (not replaced), allowing adjacent characters to be handled by collapse/trim rules
    71→
    72→**Examples**:
    73→- Input: `"Hello, World!"` → Output: `"hello-world"`
    74→- Input: `"user@example.com"` → Output: `"userexamplecom"`
    75→- Input: `"Price: $99.99"` → Output: `"price-9999"`
    76→
    77→---
    78→
    79→### REQ-004: Hyphen Collapse [Must Have]
    80→**User**: Developer using the utility module
    81→**Need**: Consolidate multiple consecutive hyphens into a single hyphen
    82→**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens reduce readability and create unnecessarily long slugs; single hyphens are cleaner and more professional
    83→
    84→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    85→- Two or more consecutive hyphens are replaced with a single hyphen
    86→- This applies after space/underscore replacement and special character removal
    87→- Single hyphens remain unchanged
    88→
    89→**Examples**:

    93→

    95→
    96→### REQ-005: Leading and Trailing Hyphen Removal [Must Have]
    97→**User**: Developer using the utility module
    98→**Need**: Remove hyphens from the beginning and end of the slug
    99→**Rationale**: Slugs should start and end with meaningful content (letters or numbers), not separators, for cleaner appearance and better usability

   107→**Examples**:

   109→- Input: `"--start"` → Output: `"start"`
   110→- Input: `"end--"` → Output: `"end"`
   111→- Input: `" --- "` → Output: `""`
   112→
   113→---
   114→
   115→### REQ-006: Transformation Order [Must Have]
   116→**User**: Developer using the utility module
   117→**Need**: Apply transformations in the correct sequence to achieve expected results
   118→**Rationale**: The order of operations affects the final output; a defined sequence ensures predictable behavior
   119→
   120→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   121→- Transformations are applied in this order:
   122→  1. Convert to lowercase
   123→  2. Replace spaces and underscores with hyphens
   124→  3. Remove non-alphanumeric characters (except hyphens)
   125→  4. Collapse repeated hyphens
   126→  5. Trim leading and trailing hyphens
   127→- The function produces correct output for all provided examples
   128→
   129→**Examples** (complete transformation):
   130→- Input: `"Hello, World!"` → `"hello, world!"` → `"hello,-world!"` → `"hello-world"` → `"hello-world"` → `"hello-world"`
   131→- Input: `"Foo__Bar"` → `"foo__bar"` → `"foo--bar"` → `"foo--bar"` → `"foo-bar"` → `"foo-bar"`
   132→- Input: `" a---b "` → `" a---b "` → `"--a---b--"` → `"--a---b--"` → `"-a-b-"` → `"a-b"`
   133→
   134→## User Stories
   135→
   136→### STORY-001: Generate URL Slug from Title
   137→**As a** developer building a content management feature
   138→**I want** to convert article titles into URL-safe slugs
   139→**So that** I can create clean, readable URLs for published content
   140→
   141→**Acceptance Scenarios**:
   142→```gherkin
   143→GIVEN I have an article title "Hello, World!"
   144→WHEN I call slugify("Hello, World!")
   145→THEN I receive "hello-world"
   146→
   147→GIVEN I have a title with underscores "Foo__Bar"
   148→WHEN I call slugify("Foo__Bar")
   149→THEN I receive "foo-bar"
   150→
   151→GIVEN I have a title with multiple hyphens "a---b"
   152→WHEN I call slugify("a---b")
   153→THEN I receive "a-b"
   154→```
   155→
   156→---
   157→
   158→### STORY-002: Handle Edge Cases Gracefully
   159→**As a** developer using the slugify utility
   160→**I want** the function to handle edge cases without errors
   161→**So that** I can rely on it for any text input without special error handling
   162→
   163→**Acceptance Scenarios**:
   164→```gherkin
   165→GIVEN I have empty input ""
   166→WHEN I call slugify("")
   167→THEN I receive ""
   168→
   169→GIVEN I have whitespace-only input "   "
   170→WHEN I call slugify("   ")
   171→THEN I receive ""
   172→
   173→GIVEN I have special characters only "!@#$%"
   174→WHEN I call slugify("!@#$%")
   175→THEN I receive ""
   176→
   177→GIVEN I have leading/trailing spaces "  hello  "
   178→WHEN I call slugify("  hello  ")
   179→THEN I receive "hello"
   180→```
   181→
   182→## Non-Functional Requirements
   183→
   184→### NFR-001: Performance [Should Have]
   185→**Requirement**: The slugify function should process typical input strings (< 500 characters) in under 10ms
   186→**Rationale**: String utility functions are often called frequently; reasonable performance prevents bottlenecks
   187→**Acceptance**: Benchmark tests confirm processing time meets threshold for typical use cases
   188→
   189→### NFR-002: Testability [Must Have]
   190→**Requirement**: The function must be pure (no side effects) and easily testable with the provided examples
   191→**Rationale**: Pure functions are easier to test, debug, and maintain
   192→**Acceptance**: Unit tests can verify all requirements and examples without mocking or complex setup
   193→
   194→### NFR-003: Code Quality [Should Have]
   195→**Requirement**: Implementation should follow project TypeScript conventions and be maintainable
   196→**Rationale**: Consistent code quality supports long-term maintainability
   197→**Acceptance**: Code passes linting, follows naming conventions, and includes appropriate type annotations
   198→
   199→## Constraints
   200→
   201→### Technical Constraints
   202→- Implementation must be in TypeScript
   203→- Function must be added to the existing `src/utils.ts` module
   204→- Must be compatible with Bun runtime
   205→- Must not introduce external dependencies
   206→
   207→### Business Constraints
   208→- Must handle all provided examples correctly
   209→- Must be a pure function with no side effects
   210→- Must be backward-compatible with existing utility module structure
   211→
   212→## Dependencies
   213→
   214→### Internal Dependencies
   215→- Utility module (`src/utils.ts`) must exist and be extensible
   216→- Test infrastructure (`bun test`) must be available for validation
   217→
   218→### External Dependencies
   219→- None required (standard JavaScript string methods are sufficient)
   220→
   221→## Out of Scope
   222→
   223→The following are explicitly excluded from this feature:
   224→
   225→- **Custom separator configuration**: The hyphen is the fixed separator; no option to use underscores or other characters
   226→- **Unicode normalization**: Advanced Unicode handling (e.g., converting accented characters to ASCII equivalents) is not required
   227→- **Maximum length enforcement**: No truncation or length limiting
   228→- **Uniqueness guarantees**: The function does not ensure globally unique slugs or handle collisions
   229→- **Internationalization**: No locale-specific transformations or right-to-left text support
   230→- **Database integration**: No automatic slug persistence or collision detection
   231→- **URL encoding**: The function produces clean slugs but does not perform percent-encoding
   232→
   233→## Validation Examples

   236→
   237→| Input | Expected Output | Rule Tested |

     8→
     9→# Feature Requirements: slugify-utility
    10→
    11→## Overview
    12→
    13→### Purpose
    14→Provide a string utility function that converts arbitrary text into URL-safe, human-readable slugs suitable for use in web addresses, file names, and identifiers.
    15→
    16→### Business Context
    17→Slugs are essential for creating clean, SEO-friendly URLs and consistent identifiers across the application. This utility will standardize text transformation logic, ensuring consistent slug generation throughout the codebase and reducing duplicate implementation.
    18→
    19→### Success Criteria
    20→- A single, reusable slugify function is available in the utility module
    21→- All edge cases (spaces, underscores, special characters, repeated hyphens) are handled correctly
    22→- Function behavior matches the specified transformation rules exactly
    23→- The implementation is testable and maintainable
    24→
    25→## Functional Requirements
    26→
    27→### REQ-001: Text Normalization [Must Have]
    28→**User**: Developer using the utility module
    29→**Need**: Convert arbitrary text strings into normalized lowercase format
    30→**Rationale**: URLs and identifiers should be case-insensitive and follow lowercase convention for consistency and compatibility
    31→
    32→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    33→- All uppercase letters (A-Z) are converted to lowercase (a-z)
    34→- Mixed-case input produces consistent lowercase output
    35→- Non-ASCII letters retain their character but follow lowercase transformation if applicable
    36→
    37→**Examples**:
    38→- Input: `"Hello"` → Output: `"hello"`
    39→- Input: `"WORLD"` → Output: `"world"`
    40→- Input: `"MixedCase"` → Output: `"mixedcase"`
    41→
    42→---
    43→
    44→### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement [Must Have]
    45→**User**: Developer using the utility module
    46→**Need**: Replace spaces and underscores with hyphens
    47→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the standard word separator in URLs and improve readability while maintaining URL safety
    48→
    49→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    50→- All space characters (` `) are replaced with hyphens (`-`)
    51→- All underscore characters (`_`) are replaced with hyphens (`-`)
    52→- Multiple consecutive spaces/underscores are handled by the hyphen collapse rule (REQ-004)
    53→
    54→**Examples**:
    55→- Input: `"hello world"` → Output: `"hello-world"`
    56→- Input: `"foo_bar"` → Output: `"foo-bar"`
    57→- Input: `"one two three"` → Output: `"one-two-three"`
    58→
    59→---
    60→
    61→### REQ-003: Special Character Removal [Must Have]
    62→**User**: Developer using the utility module
    63→**Need**: Remove characters that are not letters, numbers, or hyphens
    64→**Rationale**: URLs and identifiers should only contain safe, alphanumeric characters plus hyphens to avoid encoding issues and ensure universal compatibility
    65→
    66→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    67→- Only alphanumeric characters (a-z, 0-9) and hyphens (`-`) are retained in the output
    68→- Punctuation marks (`!`, `?`, `.`, `,`, `;`, `:`, `'`, `"`, etc.) are removed
    69→- Special symbols (`@`, `#`, `$`, `%`, `&`, `*`, `(`, `)`, etc.) are removed
    70→- Characters are removed (not replaced), allowing adjacent characters to be handled by collapse/trim rules
    71→
    72→**Examples**:
    73→- Input: `"Hello, World!"` → Output: `"hello-world"`
    74→- Input: `"user@example.com"` → Output: `"userexamplecom"`
    75→- Input: `"Price: $99.99"` → Output: `"price-9999"`
    76→
    77→---
    78→
    79→### REQ-004: Hyphen Collapse [Must Have]
    80→**User**: Developer using the utility module
    81→**Need**: Consolidate multiple consecutive hyphens into a single hyphen
    82→**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens reduce readability and create unnecessarily long slugs; single hyphens are cleaner and more professional
    83→
    84→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    85→- Two or more consecutive hyphens are replaced with a single hyphen
    86→- This applies after space/underscore replacement and special character removal
    87→- Single hyphens remain unchanged
    88→
    89→**Examples**:
    90→- Input: `"a---b"` → Output: `"a-b"`
    91→- Input: `"foo--bar"` → Output: `"foo-bar"`
    92→- Input: `"multiple   spaces"` (becomes `"multiple---spaces"` after replacement) → Output: `"multiple-spaces"`
    93→
    94→---
    95→
    96→### REQ-005: Leading and Trailing Hyphen Removal [Must Have]
    97→**User**: Developer using the utility module
    98→**Need**: Remove hyphens from the beginning and end of the slug
    99→**Rationale**: Slugs should start and end with meaningful content (letters or numbers), not separators, for cleaner appearance and better usability
   100→
   101→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   102→- Any hyphens at the start of the string are removed
   103→- Any hyphens at the end of the string are removed
   104→- Interior hyphens are preserved
   105→- Empty or whitespace-only input may result in an empty string after processing
   106→
   107→**Examples**:
   108→- Input: `"-hello-"` → Output: `"hello"`
   109→- Input: `"--start"` → Output: `"start"`
   110→- Input: `"end--"` → Output: `"end"`
   111→- Input: `" --- "` → Output: `""`
   112→
   113→---
   114→
   115→### REQ-006: Transformation Order [Must Have]
   116→**User**: Developer using the utility module
   117→**Need**: Apply transformations in the correct sequence to achieve expected results
   118→**Rationale**: The order of operations affects the final output; a defined sequence ensures predictable behavior
   119→
   120→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   121→- Transformations are applied in this order:
   122→  1. Convert to lowercase
   123→  2. Replace spaces and underscores with hyphens
   124→  3. Remove non-alphanumeric characters (except hyphens)
   125→  4. Collapse repeated hyphens
   126→  5. Trim leading and trailing hyphens
   127→- The function produces correct output for all provided examples
   128→
   129→**Examples** (complete transformation):
   130→- Input: `"Hello, World!"` → `"hello, world!"` → `"hello,-world!"` → `"hello-world"` → `"hello-world"` → `"hello-world"`
   131→- Input: `"Foo__Bar"` → `"foo__bar"` → `"foo--bar"` → `"foo--bar"` → `"foo-bar"` → `"foo-bar"`
   132→- Input: `" a---b "` → `" a---b "` → `"--a---b--"` → `"--a---b--"` → `"-a-b-"` → `"a-b"`
   133→
   134→## User Stories
   135→
   136→### STORY-001: Generate URL Slug from Title
   137→**As a** developer building a content management feature
   138→**I want** to convert article titles into URL-safe slugs
   139→**So that** I can create clean, readable URLs for published content
   140→
   141→**Acceptance Scenarios**:

   143→GIVEN I have an article title "Hello, World!"
   144→WHEN I call slugify("Hello, World!")
   145→THEN I receive "hello-world"
   146→
   147→GIVEN I have a title with underscores "Foo__Bar"
   148→WHEN I call slugify("Foo__Bar")
   149→THEN I receive "foo-bar"
   150→
   151→GIVEN I have a title with multiple hyphens "a---b"
   152→WHEN I call slugify("a---b")
   153→THEN I receive "a-b"
   154→```
   155→
   156→---
   157→
   158→### STORY-002: Handle Edge Cases Gracefully
   159→**As a** developer using the slugify utility
   160→**I want** the function to handle edge cases without errors
   161→**So that** I can rely on it for any text input without special error handling
   162→
   163→**Acceptance Scenarios**:
   164→```gherkin
   165→GIVEN I have empty input ""
   166→WHEN I call slugify("")
   167→THEN I receive ""
   168→
   169→GIVEN I have whitespace-only input "   "
   170→WHEN I call slugify("   ")
   171→THEN I receive ""
   172→
   173→GIVEN I have special characters only "!@#$%"
   174→WHEN I call slugify("!@#$%")
   175→THEN I receive ""
   176→
   177→GIVEN I have leading/trailing spaces "  hello  "
   178→WHEN I call slugify("  hello  ")
   179→THEN I receive "hello"
   180→```
   181→
   182→## Non-Functional Requirements
   183→
   184→### NFR-001: Performance [Should Have]
   185→**Requirement**: The slugify function should process typical input strings (< 500 characters) in under 10ms
   186→**Rationale**: String utility functions are often called frequently; reasonable performance prevents bottlenecks
   187→**Acceptance**: Benchmark tests confirm processing time meets threshold for typical use cases
   188→
   189→### NFR-002: Testability [Must Have]
   190→**Requirement**: The function must be pure (no side effects) and easily testable with the provided examples
   191→**Rationale**: Pure functions are easier to test, debug, and maintain
   192→**Acceptance**: Unit tests can verify all requirements and examples without mocking or complex setup
   193→
   194→### NFR-003: Code Quality [Should Have]
   195→**Requirement**: Implementation should follow project TypeScript conventions and be maintainable
   196→**Rationale**: Consistent code quality supports long-term maintainability
   197→**Acceptance**: Code passes linting, follows naming conventions, and includes appropriate type annotations
   198→
   199→## Constraints
   200→
   201→### Technical Constraints
   202→- Implementation must be in TypeScript
   203→- Function must be added to the existing `src/utils.ts` module
   204→- Must be compatible with Bun runtime
   205→- Must not introduce external dependencies
   206→
   207→### Business Constraints

   211→
   212→## Dependencies

   221→## Out of Scope
