     9→# Feature Requirements: slugify-utility
    10→
    11→## Overview
    12→
    13→### Purpose
    14→Provide a string utility function that converts arbitrary text into URL-safe, human-readable slugs suitable for use in web addresses, file names, and identifiers.
    15→
    16→### Business Context
    17→Slugs are essential for creating clean, SEO-friendly URLs and consistent identifiers across the application. This utility will standardize text transformation logic, ensuring consistent slug generation throughout the codebase and reducing duplicate implementation.
    18→
    19→### Success Criteria
    20→- A single, reusable slugify function is available in the utility module
    21→- All edge cases (spaces, underscores, special characters, repeated hyphens) are handled correctly
    22→- Function behavior matches the specified transformation rules exactly
    23→- The implementation is testable and maintainable
    24→
    25→## Functional Requirements
    26→
    27→### REQ-001: Text Normalization [Must Have]
    28→**User**: Developer using the utility module
    29→**Need**: Convert arbitrary text strings into normalized lowercase format
    30→**Rationale**: URLs and identifiers should be case-insensitive and follow lowercase convention for consistency and compatibility
    31→
    32→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    33→- All uppercase letters (A-Z) are converted to lowercase (a-z)
    34→- Mixed-case input produces consistent lowercase output
    35→- Non-ASCII letters retain their character but follow lowercase transformation if applicable
    36→
    37→**Examples**:
    38→- Input: `"Hello"` → Output: `"hello"`
    39→- Input: `"WORLD"` → Output: `"world"`
    40→- Input: `"MixedCase"` → Output: `"mixedcase"`
    41→
    42→---
    43→
    44→### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement [Must Have]
    45→**User**: Developer using the utility module
    46→**Need**: Replace spaces and underscores with hyphens
    47→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the standard word separator in URLs and improve readability while maintaining URL safety
    48→
    49→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    50→- All space characters (` `) are replaced with hyphens (`-`)
    51→- All underscore characters (`_`) are replaced with hyphens (`-`)
    52→- Multiple consecutive spaces/underscores are handled by the hyphen collapse rule (REQ-004)
    53→
    54→**Examples**:
    55→- Input: `"hello world"` → Output: `"hello-world"`
    56→- Input: `"foo_bar"` → Output: `"foo-bar"`
    57→- Input: `"one two three"` → Output: `"one-two-three"`
    58→
    59→---
    60→
    61→### REQ-003: Special Character Removal [Must Have]
    62→**User**: Developer using the utility module
    63→**Need**: Remove characters that are not letters, numbers, or hyphens
    64→**Rationale**: URLs and identifiers should only contain safe, alphanumeric characters plus hyphens to avoid encoding issues and ensure universal compatibility
    65→
    66→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    67→- Only alphanumeric characters (a-z, 0-9) and hyphens (`-`) are retained in the output
    68→- Punctuation marks (`!`, `?`, `.`, `,`, `;`, `:`, `'`, `"`, etc.) are removed
    69→- Special symbols (`@`, `#`, `$`, `%`, `&`, `*`, `(`, `)`, etc.) are removed
    70→- Characters are removed (not replaced), allowing adjacent characters to be handled by collapse/trim rules
    71→
    72→**Examples**:
    73→- Input: `"Hello, World!"` → Output: `"hello-world"`
    74→- Input: `"user@example.com"` → Output: `"userexamplecom"`
    75→- Input: `"Price: $99.99"` → Output: `"price-9999"`
    76→
    77→---
    78→
    79→### REQ-004: Hyphen Collapse [Must Have]
    80→**User**: Developer using the utility module
    81→**Need**: Consolidate multiple consecutive hyphens into a single hyphen
    82→**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens reduce readability and create unnecessarily long slugs; single hyphens are cleaner and more professional
    83→
    84→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    85→- Two or more consecutive hyphens are replaced with a single hyphen
    86→- This applies after space/underscore replacement and special character removal
    87→- Single hyphens remain unchanged
    88→
    89→**Examples**:
    90→- Input: `"a---b"` → Output: `"a-b"`
    91→- Input: `"foo--bar"` → Output: `"foo-bar"`
    92→- Input: `"multiple   spaces"` (becomes `"multiple---spaces"` after replacement) → Output: `"multiple-spaces"`
    93→
    94→---
    95→
    96→### REQ-005: Leading and Trailing Hyphen Removal [Must Have]
    97→**User**: Developer using the utility module
    98→**Need**: Remove hyphens from the beginning and end of the slug
    99→**Rationale**: Slugs should start and end with meaningful content (letters or numbers), not separators, for cleaner appearance and better usability
   100→
   101→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   102→- Any hyphens at the start of the string are removed
   103→- Any hyphens at the end of the string are removed
   104→- Interior hyphens are preserved
   105→- Empty or whitespace-only input may result in an empty string after processing
   106→
   107→**Examples**:
   108→- Input: `"-hello-"` → Output: `"hello"`
   109→- Input: `"--start"` → Output: `"start"`
   110→- Input: `"end--"` → Output: `"end"`
   111→- Input: `" --- "` → Output: `""`
   112→
   113→---
   114→
   115→### REQ-006: Transformation Order [Must Have]
   116→**User**: Developer using the utility module
   117→**Need**: Apply transformations in the correct sequence to achieve expected results
   118→**Rationale**: The order of operations affects the final output; a defined sequence ensures predictable behavior
   119→
   120→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   121→- Transformations are applied in this order:
   122→  1. Convert to lowercase
   123→  2. Replace spaces and underscores with hyphens
   124→  3. Remove non-alphanumeric characters (except hyphens)
   125→  4. Collapse repeated hyphens
   126→  5. Trim leading and trailing hyphens
   127→- The function produces correct output for all provided examples
   128→
   129→**Examples** (complete transformation):

   131→- Input: `"Foo__Bar"` → `"foo__bar"` → `"foo--bar"` → `"foo--bar"` → `"foo-bar"` → `"foo-bar"`
   132→- Input: `" a---b "` → `" a---b "` → `"--a---b--"` → `"--a---b--"` → `"-a-b-"` → `"a-b"`
   133→
   134→## User Stories
   135→
   136→### STORY-001: Generate URL Slug from Title
   137→**As a** developer building a content management feature
   138→**I want** to convert article titles into URL-safe slugs
   139→**So that** I can create clean, readable URLs for published content
   140→
   141→**Acceptance Scenarios**:
   142→```gherkin
   143→GIVEN I have an article title "Hello, World!"
   144→WHEN I call slugify("Hello, World!")
   145→THEN I receive "hello-world"
   146→
   147→GIVEN I have a title with underscores "Foo__Bar"
   148→WHEN I call slugify("Foo__Bar")
   149→THEN I receive "foo-bar"
   150→
   151→GIVEN I have a title with multiple hyphens "a---b"
   152→WHEN I call slugify("a---b")
   153→THEN I receive "a-b"
   154→```
   155→
   156→---
   157→
   158→### STORY-002: Handle Edge Cases Gracefully
   159→**As a** developer using the slugify utility
   160→**I want** the function to handle edge cases without errors
   161→**So that** I can rely on it for any text input without special error handling
   162→
   163→**Acceptance Scenarios**:

   185→**Requirement**: The slugify function should process typical input strings (< 500 characters) in under 10ms
   186→**Rationale**: String utility functions are often called frequently; reasonable performance prevents bottlenecks

   204→- Must be compatible with Bun runtime

     9→# Feature Requirements: slugify-utility
    10→
    11→## Overview
    12→
    13→### Purpose
    14→Provide a string utility function that converts arbitrary text into URL-safe, human-readable slugs suitable for use in web addresses, file names, and identifiers.
    15→
    16→### Business Context
    17→Slugs are essential for creating clean, SEO-friendly URLs and consistent identifiers across the application. This utility will standardize text transformation logic, ensuring consistent slug generation throughout the codebase and reducing duplicate implementation.
    18→
    19→### Success Criteria
    20→- A single, reusable slugify function is available in the utility module
    21→- All edge cases (spaces, underscores, special characters, repeated hyphens) are handled correctly
    22→- Function behavior matches the specified transformation rules exactly
    23→- The implementation is testable and maintainable
    24→
    25→## Functional Requirements
    26→
    27→### REQ-001: Text Normalization [Must Have]
    28→**User**: Developer using the utility module
    29→**Need**: Convert arbitrary text strings into normalized lowercase format
    30→**Rationale**: URLs and identifiers should be case-insensitive and follow lowercase convention for consistency and compatibility
    31→
    32→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    33→- All uppercase letters (A-Z) are converted to lowercase (a-z)
    34→- Mixed-case input produces consistent lowercase output
    35→- Non-ASCII letters retain their character but follow lowercase transformation if applicable
    36→
    37→**Examples**:
    38→- Input: `"Hello"` → Output: `"hello"`
    39→- Input: `"WORLD"` → Output: `"world"`
    40→- Input: `"MixedCase"` → Output: `"mixedcase"`
    41→
    42→---
    43→
    44→### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement [Must Have]
    45→**User**: Developer using the utility module
    46→**Need**: Replace spaces and underscores with hyphens
    47→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the standard word separator in URLs and improve readability while maintaining URL safety
    48→
    49→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    50→- All space characters (` `) are replaced with hyphens (`-`)
    51→- All underscore characters (`_`) are replaced with hyphens (`-`)
    52→- Multiple consecutive spaces/underscores are handled by the hyphen collapse rule (REQ-004)
    53→
    54→**Examples**:
    55→- Input: `"hello world"` → Output: `"hello-world"`
    56→- Input: `"foo_bar"` → Output: `"foo-bar"`
    57→- Input: `"one two three"` → Output: `"one-two-three"`
    58→
    59→---
    60→
    61→### REQ-003: Special Character Removal [Must Have]
    62→**User**: Developer using the utility module
    63→**Need**: Remove characters that are not letters, numbers, or hyphens
    64→**Rationale**: URLs and identifiers should only contain safe, alphanumeric characters plus hyphens to avoid encoding issues and ensure universal compatibility
    65→
    66→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    67→- Only alphanumeric characters (a-z, 0-9) and hyphens (`-`) are retained in the output
    68→- Punctuation marks (`!`, `?`, `.`, `,`, `;`, `:`, `'`, `"`, etc.) are removed
    69→- Special symbols (`@`, `#`, `$`, `%`, `&`, `*`, `(`, `)`, etc.) are removed
    70→- Characters are removed (not replaced), allowing adjacent characters to be handled by collapse/trim rules
    71→
    72→**Examples**:
    73→- Input: `"Hello, World!"` → Output: `"hello-world"`
    74→- Input: `"user@example.com"` → Output: `"userexamplecom"`
    75→- Input: `"Price: $99.99"` → Output: `"price-9999"`
    76→
    77→---
    78→
    79→### REQ-004: Hyphen Collapse [Must Have]
    80→**User**: Developer using the utility module
    81→**Need**: Consolidate multiple consecutive hyphens into a single hyphen
    82→**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens reduce readability and create unnecessarily long slugs; single hyphens are cleaner and more professional
    83→
    84→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    85→- Two or more consecutive hyphens are replaced with a single hyphen
    86→- This applies after space/underscore replacement and special character removal
    87→- Single hyphens remain unchanged
    88→
    89→**Examples**:
    90→- Input: `"a---b"` → Output: `"a-b"`
    91→- Input: `"foo--bar"` → Output: `"foo-bar"`
    92→- Input: `"multiple   spaces"` (becomes `"multiple---spaces"` after replacement) → Output: `"multiple-spaces"`
    93→
    94→---
    95→
    96→### REQ-005: Leading and Trailing Hyphen Removal [Must Have]
    97→**User**: Developer using the utility module
    98→**Need**: Remove hyphens from the beginning and end of the slug
    99→**Rationale**: Slugs should start and end with meaningful content (letters or numbers), not separators, for cleaner appearance and better usability
   100→
   101→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   102→- Any hyphens at the start of the string are removed
   103→- Any hyphens at the end of the string are removed
   104→- Interior hyphens are preserved
   105→- Empty or whitespace-only input may result in an empty string after processing
   106→
   107→**Examples**:
   108→- Input: `"-hello-"` → Output: `"hello"`
   109→- Input: `"--start"` → Output: `"start"`
   110→- Input: `"end--"` → Output: `"end"`
   111→- Input: `" --- "` → Output: `""`
   112→

   114→
   115→### REQ-006: Transformation Order [Must Have]
   116→**User**: Developer using the utility module
   117→**Need**: Apply transformations in the correct sequence to achieve expected results
   118→**Rationale**: The order of operations affects the final output; a defined sequence ensures predictable behavior
   119→
   120→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   121→- Transformations are applied in this order:
   122→  1. Convert to lowercase
   123→  2. Replace spaces and underscores with hyphens
   124→  3. Remove non-alphanumeric characters (except hyphens)
   125→  4. Collapse repeated hyphens
   126→  5. Trim leading and trailing hyphens
   127→- The function produces correct output for all provided examples

   132→- Input: `" a---b "` → `" a---b "` → `"--a---b--"` → `"--a---b--"` → `"-a-b-"` → `"a-b"`
   133→
   134→## User Stories
   135→
   136→### STORY-001: Generate URL Slug from Title
   137→**As a** developer building a content management feature
   138→**I want** to convert article titles into URL-safe slugs
   139→**So that** I can create clean, readable URLs for published content

   146→

   148→WHEN I call slugify("Foo__Bar")
   149→THEN I receive "foo-bar"
   150→
   151→GIVEN I have a title with multiple hyphens "a---b"
   152→WHEN I call slugify("a---b")
   153→THEN I receive "a-b"
   154→```
   155→
   156→---
   157→
   158→### STORY-002: Handle Edge Cases Gracefully
   159→**As a** developer using the slugify utility
   160→**I want** the function to handle edge cases without errors
   161→**So that** I can rely on it for any text input without special error handling

   176→
   177→GIVEN I have leading/trailing spaces "  hello  "

   180→```

   185→**Requirement**: The slugify function should process typical input strings (< 500 characters) in under 10ms
   186→**Rationale**: String utility functions are often called frequently; reasonable performance prevents bottlenecks

   204→- Must be compatible with Bun runtime
